newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Former Afghan communist leader Karmal dies.
newsitem.headline: Former Afghan communist leader Karmal dies.

text.p: Former Afghan communist leader Babrak Karmal, installed by the Kremlin at the start of its ill-fated nine-year intervention in Afghanistan, has died in Moscow of liver cancer, Interfax news agency said on Thursday.
Karmal, 67, was in Moscow's elite Central Clinical Hospital.
Moscow-based Afghan journalist Iskander Khatmani, who had close links with Karmal, told Reuters by phone that the former leader died on Tuesday.
Officials in Moscow were not immediately available for comment.

The Kremlin put Karmal in charge of Afghanistan in December 1979 when its troops invaded the mountainous country and Soviet commandos killed the then leader Hafizullah Amin during the storming of his residence in the capital Kabul.
In November 1986 Karmal was replaced by former secret police chief Najibullah as the war against Western-backed Islamic guerrillas showed no sign of ending.
Since then, Karmal had spent most of his time in Moscow.

Khatmani said Karmal was likely to be flown for burial to northern Afghanistan, controlled by Uzbek warlord Rashid Dostum who had helped him in the past. He could not say when the burial might take place.
